prompt:
Research the official free-tier limits of the GitHub Actions service for public and private repositories (minutes, storage, concurrency). Cite the GitHub documentation page you used.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

If you're not sure about something, just say so.

response.content:
Based on the official GitHub documentation, the free-tier limits for GitHub Actions differ significantly between public and private repositories, particularly regarding billing for compute minutes. Below is a breakdown of the limits for minutes, storage, and concurrency.

### Public Repositories
For public repositories, the use of standard GitHub-hosted runners is free and unlimited in terms of minutes. However, specific resource limits still apply to ensure system stability.

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions | QUOTE: "GitHub Actions usage is **free** for **self-hosted runners** and for **public repositories** that use standard GitHub-hosted runners." | CLAIM: Public repositories using standard GitHub-hosted runners do not consume paid minutes or quota.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits | QUOTE: "Each repository is limited to events triggering a workflow run." | CLAIM: There is a rate limit of 1500 workflow trigger events per 10 seconds per repository.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits | QUOTE: "When the limit is reached, the workflow runs that were supposed to be triggered by the webhook events will be blocked and will not be queued." | CLAIM: If the trigger event rate limit is exceeded, additional workflows are blocked rather than queued.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits | QUOTE: "A check suite can have a maximum of 50,000 check runs." | CLAIM: There is a hard limit of 50,000 check runs per check suite for both API-created and Action-created runs.

### Private Repositories (Free Tier Plans)
For private repositories, GitHub provides a monthly quota of free minutes and storage based on the account plan (Free, Pro, Team, or Enterprise). Usage beyond these quotas is billed.

**Minutes and Storage Quotas:**

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions | QUOTE: "For **private repositories**, each GitHub account receives a quota of free minutes, artifact storage, and cache storage for use with GitHub-hosted runners, depending on the account's plan." | CLAIM: Private repositories have specific monthly quotas for minutes and storage based on the plan type.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions | QUOTE: "| GitHub Free | 500 MB | 2,000 | 10 GB | Not applicable |" | CLAIM: The GitHub Free plan includes 2,000 free minutes per month, 500 MB of artifact storage, and 10 GB of cache storage per repository.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions | QUOTE: "| GitHub Pro | 1 GB | 3,000 | 10 GB | Not applicable |" | CLAIM: The GitHub Pro plan includes 3,000 free minutes per month, 1 GB of artifact storage, and 10 GB of cache storage per repository.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions | QUOTE: "The storage amounts shown are **shared** with GitHub Packages. This means your total storage across Actions artifacts, Actions caches, and Packages cannot exceed the included amount for your plan." | CLAIM: Artifact storage limits are shared with GitHub Packages storage, while cache storage is a separate allowance.

**Concurrency Limits for Private Repositories (Standard Runners):**
Concurrency limits depend on the plan type. These limits apply to the number of jobs that can run simultaneously.

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits | QUOTE: "| Standard GitHub-hosted runner | Free | 20 | 5 | Not applicable |" | CLAIM: The GitHub Free plan allows up to 20 total concurrent jobs and a maximum of 5 concurrent macOS jobs on standard runners.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits | QUOTE: "| Standard GitHub-hosted runner | Pro | 40 | 5 | Not applicable |" | CLAIM: The GitHub Pro plan allows up to 40 total concurrent jobs and a maximum of 5 concurrent macOS jobs on standard runners.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits | QUOTE: "The maximum concurrent macOS jobs is shared across standard GitHub-hosted runners and GitHub-hosted larger runners." | CLAIM: The limit for concurrent macOS jobs is a pooled resource across both standard and larger runner types.

### General Execution and Queue Limits
These limits apply to all repositories regardless of visibility or plan.

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits | QUOTE: "Each job in a workflow can run for up to 6 hours of execution time. If a job reaches this limit, the job is terminated and fails." | CLAIM: Standard GitHub-hosted runner jobs have a maximum execution time of 6 hours.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits | QUOTE: "When using `queue: max` in the `concurrency` section, up to 100 jobs or workflow runs can be queued per concurrency group." | CLAIM: There is a limit of 100 queued runs per concurrency group when using the `queue: max` setting.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits | QUOTE: "500 workflow runs / 10 seconds" | CLAIM: There is a global limit of 500 workflow runs that can be queued every 10 seconds.

### Important Notes on "Free" Usage
*   **Larger Runners:** Even for public repositories, larger runners are not free.
    SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions | QUOTE: "Larger runners are always charged for, even when used by public repositories or when you have quota available from your plan." | CLAIM: Usage of larger runners incurs costs regardless of repository visibility or remaining free tier quota.
*   **Self-Hosted Runners:** These are free to use in terms of GitHub billing (you pay for your own infrastructure).
    SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions | QUOTE: "GitHub Actions usage is **free** for **self-hosted runners**..." | CLAIM: Using self-hosted runners does not consume GitHub Actions minutes or incur GitHub billing charges.
